report.summary: Analyzed SQLite WAL synchronous=NORMAL durability. Process crash: no corruption; recent commits safe if OS cache intact, but not guaranteed. OS crash/power loss: database safe from corruption (WAL checksums), but transactions since last checkpoint may be lost. Network shares/OneDrive: unsupported, high corruption risk; WAL likely non-functional. Recommendation: use only on local disk; implement proactive checkpoints; reject network paths.
risks: Data loss window on OS crash proportional to checkpoint interval
Network/cloud paths (including OneDrive) cause corruption; WAL mode may fail entirely
OneDrive may corrupt file during sync or rename operations
Windows network shares may not support required byte-range locking
todos: Enforce local storage only for SQLite databases; detect and block network/cloud paths
Use journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL for performance
Implement periodic checkpointing (e.g., after N writes or time-based) to reduce loss window
If durability is critical, consider synchronous=FULL
Add integrity check on database open (PRAGMA integrity_check)
If network paths are unavoidable, design a server-based storage instead

handoff.suggestion: For Daedalus: in database initialization, check path is local (e.g., using pathlib and win32api to detect UNC/DriveType) and refuse network/cloud paths. Set PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;. After every ~100 write transactions or 30 seconds, run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) to flush data and limit potential loss on crash. Include startup integrity check. This balances performance and safety for local-only operation.

name: q04-sqlite-wal-durability
question: SQLite with journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL: what exactly is guaranteed across a process crash, an OS crash and power loss, and how do those guarantees change on a network share or a OneDrive-synced path?
